text:
Lina: POC note -- Cust: Meridian Financial. They want PrivateDeploy with connector in their VPC and strict egress controls. Need one-page acceptance + short runbook. Can someone draft? @Marco @Aisha
Marco: Ill draft. Quick confirm: they require (1) preservation of client src IP for log correlation, (2) allowlisting of static egress IPs, and (3) optional TLS-inspect in their proxy?
Aisha: Correct on all three. Also they will insist on an operator-accessible egress kill switch and proof of KMS integration for key wrapping.
Ben: Re topology we should suggest PrivateLink interface endpoints to the management/control plane avoids internet egress. Fallback: VPC peering + TGW if they block interface endpoints.
Lina: Make the doc explicit about pros/cons. Merits: PrivateLink = least outbound surface; Peering = simpler route tables but requires NAT for model egress.
Marco: Minimal firewall/egress snippet for their network team (outbound from connector hosts):
```
# Outbound TLS to Redwood model endpoints
ALLOW tcp 443 to redwood-control-<region>.redwood-hosted.net
# DNS (if using customer resolver)
ALLOW udp 53 to <customer-dns>
# NTP
ALLOW udp 123 to 0.pool.ntp.org
# If PrivateLink: allow the interface endpoint ENI IPs we supply
# If peering: allow egress to Redwood public model IPs (we will provide ASN/IP list)
```
Aisha: Also note: if they inspect TLS SNI, they must allow SNI passthrough to preserve hostname. If they perform TLS interception, we need mutual TLS between connector and their proxy, or an allowlist of subjectAltNames for cert pinning.
Ben: For source IP preservation callout: configure connector subnet route to proxy without SNAT. If using NAT gateway before proxy, client IPs will be lost.
Marco: Add these tests in the ops runbook:
- curl health check to local connector (with --resolve)
- tcpdump on proxy to confirm client src IP
- openssl s_client -connect <proxy>:443 -servername api.redwood-hosted.net to validate SNI passthrough
- traceroute to ensure route path
ops-bot: Tip: use the smoke command after allowlist applied:
```
curl -v https://api.redwood-hosted.net/healthz --resolve "api.redwood-hosted.net:443:<connector-ip>"
```
Aisha: Security questionnaire bullets (short):
- Data in transit: TLS 1.2+ enforced, TLS 1.3 recommended
- Key mgmt: Option A: customer KMS integration (HSM-backed) OR Option B: Redwood-managed keys with attestation report
- Audit logs: syslog/s3 delivery options, retention 30/90/365d (customer selectable)
- Access controls: RBAC + MFA for operator UI; operator kill switch logged and auditable
Lina: Pricing note for sales: PrivateDeploy base + infra fee. If customer requires stable egress IPs and dedicated GPU pools, recommend reserved-capacity add-on (discounted with 12mo commit). Marco, please insert exact numbers in the proposal doc.
Marco: Will do. Also include a short sentence: "If customer cannot permit interface endpoints, we can deploy via peering but egress will require NAT or proxying through their perimeter, which may affect client IP preservation and SNI behavior."
Ben: One more ops tip: provide sample iptables rule to preserve IP on the proxy host (for their ops):
```
# on proxy host to accept forwarded src ip
iptables -t nat -A PREROUTING -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
```
Aisha: For the kill switch we propose a simple operator command that blackholes egress routes in route table + notifies oncall. Document both manual and automated options.
Lina: Keep it to 1 page checklist + 1 page runbook. I want to send to Meridian by COB.
Marco: Draft ready in ~60m, will paste here for review.
Lina: Thanks team :thumbsup:
